The restored single-terminal hypothesis repairs the earlier global corollary, and the companion’s arbitrary-feasible correction has the correct sign, weight, and ownership convention.The new family establishes the stated rule obstruction: after joining the relevant interval pairs, there are  $k-r$  joint components meeting the first boundary and  $2k-r$  meeting either boundary, despite the connector graph having no cycles. Its packet surplus nevertheless exceeds the target by exactly the positive quantity in (9).I found no remaining mathematical defect requiring revision. The conclusions below concern the written proofs and the supplied, previously accepted uniqueness/freezing dependencies. They do not certify the reported checker or Lean execution.1. The earlier REVISE is fully resolvedThe first note now confines its global coefficient-one corollary to the setting in which every endpoint has at least three occupied neighbors. That is the missing hypothesis identified in the earlier review.The accompanying receiver-disjointness argument is correct. If two distinct global endpoint components meet one physical  $2\times2$  tile, their endpoints cannot be adjacent, since an endpoint edge would connect the components. They therefore occupy opposite corners. Neither remaining corner can be an endpoint, because it would join the components, or a selection, because it would have two occupied neighbors. Those corners are consequently blank. Each diagonal endpoint then has occupied degree at most two, contradicting the restored hypothesis.The packet assumptions are also now adequate:Packets are disjoint unions of original physical tiles.Every original receiver meeting a packet is contained wholly in that packet.Outside component charges and endpoint-free deficits are counted only outside the packets.These conditions justify the displayed additive global ledger. In particular, they prevent an outside receiver from sharing a tile with a packet.The stronger assumption has been confined to the correct place. The contraction and local ledger in §§1–2 still require only feasibility, and the local target equivalence in §3 retains that generality. The no-TP–TP sufficient class still correctly requires matching closure.The unchanged neutral-family path, backward connector, and alternate-phase formulas remain correct. The first note also now explicitly assumes a finite region and correctly identifies §§1–6 as containing the general proofs. Its acceptance does not depend on the companion’s new source-collision construction.2. Companion §§1–2: the overlap correction is exact2.1 Global component labels are essential and are used correctlyLet  $K$  range over the connected components of the graph induced by the full endpoint set  $P$ . Every actual matching edge lies inside one such component. Since every endpoint has exactly one actual mate,
$$|K|=2|M_K|,$$
so each  $K$  has even cardinality.For an endpoint-bearing physical tile  $Q$ , the relevant multiplicity is
$$m_Q=\#\{K:Q\in R_K\},$$
where the labels  $K$  come from the whole endpoint graph, not from the endpoint graph restricted to  $Q$ .The classification in §1 is correct:
$$m_Q\ge2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
m_Q=2,\qquad |T\cap Q|=0,$$
and  $Q$  contains precisely two diagonal endpoints and two blanks.There cannot be a third endpoint in that tile without connecting the two components. There cannot be a selected corner in either remaining position because it would see both endpoints.The converse is correctly rejected. Two diagonal endpoints in a tile may connect through endpoints outside that tile. In that case  $m_Q=1$ , the tile occurs once in the receiver of that global component, and it contributes no overlap correction.This distinction prevents a local disconnected profile from being incorrectly charged as a receiver overlap.2.2 The union-charge correction is  $+2N$ Put  $t_Q=|T\cap Q|$ . Summing the component charges gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\sum_K\rho_K
&=\sum_K\frac{|K|}{2}
  +\sum_K\sum_{Q\in R_K}(t_Q-2)\\
&=|M|+\sum_{Q\text{ meeting }P}m_Q(t_Q-2).
\end{aligned}$$
The receiver-union charge is
$$\rho_{\rm union}
=|M|+\sum_{Q\text{ meeting }P}(t_Q-2).$$
Subtracting,
$$\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\rm union}-\sum_K\rho_K
&=\sum_{Q\text{ meeting }P}(1-m_Q)(t_Q-2)\\
&=\sum_{Q\text{ meeting }P}(m_Q-1)(2-t_Q).
\end{aligned}$$
Every nonzero term has  $m_Q=2$  and  $t_Q=0$ , so it equals  $2$ . Therefore
$$\boxed{\rho_{\rm union}=\sum_K\rho_K+2N.}$$
Both the sign and the coefficient are correct.A shared tile occurs in two receiver lists but only once in their union. Its excess multiplicity is  $m_Q-1=1$ , so the correction is two per shared tile, not four.The single-terminal specialization is also correct: the degree argument excludes every such tile, giving  $N=0$ .2.3 Packet closure gives the required ownership partitionBecause every packet is a union of whole physical tiles, a receiver tile intersecting a packet lies entirely in that packet. The receiver-closure hypothesis then puts the entire corresponding component receiver in that packet.Consequently a global endpoint component cannot be split between a packet and the outside, or between two disjoint packets. An outside receiver is disjoint from every packet.This also implies matching closure of each packet: the two endpoints of an actual matching edge belong to the same global endpoint component. $$\sum_jS_j,\qquad D_{\rm out},\qquad
-\rho_{\rm outside\ union}.$$

$$-\rho_{\rm outside\ union}
=-q+R_{\rm out}-2N_{\rm out}.$$
Hence
$$\boxed{
\frac{mn}{2}-|T|-|M|
=\sum_jS_j+D_{\rm out}-q+R_{\rm out}-2N_{\rm out}.
}$$
The subtraction of  $2N_{\rm out}$  is the necessary sign: summing overlapping component receivers makes their combined charge too favorable by two per shared tile.Overlaps inside a packet are already included in its directly computed weighted surplus  $S_j$ .
